Kuvitus: talvi-ilta ja punainen omakotit: Illustration: a winter evening and a red detached house in the snow. Light shines from the windows of the house, and smoke rises from the chimney of the sauna. On the end wall of the house there is a charging station, from which a winding charging cable runs to the charging socket below the front door of a blue electric car standing in the yard. In the background there are spruces and an electricity pole from which wires come to the roof of the house.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kodin sähkö: Diagram, not to scale: the home electrical system. At the top left a cable with three phase conductors comes from the electricity grid to the consumer unit. In the consumer unit come first the main fuses, three of them, 25 amperes each, and below them the busbars from which three circuits leave. The top circuit is three-phase, its miniature circuit breaker is 16 amperes and it feeds the electric sauna heater. The middle circuit is single-phase, 16 amperes, and it feeds the sockets of the kitchen, to which a kettle is connected. The bottom circuit is the charging station's own three-phase circuit: it has a 16 ampere miniature circuit breaker and a residual current device (RCD) with a tripping current of 30 milliamperes. The three-phase wires are drawn as three lines, the single-phase one as one.
Vaakapylväskuvaaja mittakaavassa: pääsul: Horizontal bar chart, to scale: the current passing through the main fuses in each phase conductor L1, L2 and L3 when the following are on at the same time: a 9.0 kilowatt three-phase sauna heater, a 2.0 kilowatt kettle on phase L1 and an 11 kilowatt three-phase charging station. The heater draws 13.0 amperes from each phase and the charging station 16 amperes, the kettle 8.7 amperes from phase L1. The current of phase L1 is 37.7 amperes and that of phases L2 and L3 29.0 amperes. A vertical dashed line at 25 amperes is the size of the main fuse: the bar of every phase extends past it.
Kaavakuva, malli eikä mittaus: sähköauto: Diagram, a model and not a measurement: the power P taken from the grid by the charging station of an electric car in kilowatts as a function of time t in hours, when a 64 kilowatt-hour battery is charged from a charge level of 20 percent. The power stays at 11 kilowatts for about 4.5 hours, until the charge level is 90 percent. After that the power decreases ever more slowly, and charging ends at about 6.0 hours, when the charge level is 99 percent. The area under the steady part is shaded: it is the energy taken from the grid, power times time.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: latausaseman verk: Graph, to scale: the power P taken from the grid by a charging station in kilowatts as a function of time t in hours during one charge. The vertical grid lines are at 0.5 hour intervals, the horizontal ones at 2, 4, 5.5, 8 and 11 kilowatts. The power is first 11 kilowatts for the time 0–2.0 hours, then 5.5 kilowatts for the time 2.0–3.0 hours, after which charging ends and the power is zero.
